item.title: PR Review Loop — Implementation & Operations
item.description:
Meshery PR Review Loop — Implementation & Operations

1. Overview

“When you open a PR, show you a PR you can help review.”

The Meshery PR Review Loop is an automated community collaboration mechanism designed to encourage reciprocal peer review among contributors. When an author opens a pull request (PR) in meshery/meshery, the system surfaces up to three currently open PRs that share technical context, programming language, or architectural components with their change.

item.title: PR Review Loop — Matching Design
item.description:
Meshery PR Review Loop — Matching Design

1. Goal

When a contributor opens a pull request (PR) in the meshery/meshery repository, which existing open PRs are most relevant for them to review?

The purpose of the Meshery PR Review Loop is to encourage reciprocal peer review among contributors working on similar areas of the codebase. By suggesting relevant open PRs to an author at the moment they submit code, contributors can share domain knowledge, review each other’s work, and help maintainers move changes forward faster.

item.title: PR Review Loop — Problem Statement
item.description:
Meshery PR Review Loop — Problem Statement

1. Problem

Contributors submitting pull requests (PRs) to meshery/meshery often face difficulty discovering other open pull requests that are relevant to their domain or technical focus. While many contributors are willing to participate in peer review, finding appropriate PRs among hundreds of open issues and pull requests requires manual filtering across disparate subsystems, languages, and components.

2. Why This Matters

Reciprocal review participation and effective review discovery are foundational to a healthy open source contributor experience. Maintainers frequently bear the primary burden of code reviews, leading to review queues and longer feedback cycles. When authors who are already engaged in the codebase can easily discover related work, peer review capacity increases naturally. Reviewing related contributions also helps authors familiarize themselves with adjacent subsystems and conventions across the project.
